title: Security & Compliance Integrated Guidance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exceptions
author: Aisha Khan
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational workflows for: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk/exception handling. It is intended for engineering, security, product, and compliance reviewers who operate or assess inference services (hosted, dedicated, and private deployments).

Scope & Purpose

- Scope: Applies to all production and pre-production services in the Redwood cloud and customer-managed private deployments.
- Purpose: Provide a single operational reference that defines guardrails, owners, SLOs, retention requirements, and step-by-step workflows for evidence collection and risk exceptions.

Roles & Ownership

- Security (owner): Policy design, exception approvals, audit evidence collection, yearly compliance attestations.
- Eng-Platform / Infra: Implement RBAC integrations, logging pipeline, KMS integration, and firewall/network controls.
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: Ensure runtime enforces RBAC scopes, supports KV-caching segregation, and surfaces audit hooks.
- Product & Legal: Define data residency requirements per contract and approve long-term retention requests.

Principles

1. Least privilege by default — grant minimal permissions required for a role.
2. Separation of duties — admin, deploy, and audit roles should be distinct.
3. Traceability — every privileged action must be logged with user, service, timestamp, and context.
4. Defense in depth — combine network controls, identity, and service-level checks.

RBAC & Authentication

- Services and components: redwood-identity (SSO broker), iam-policy-service (policy store), policy-evaluator (runtime), vault (secrets), kms-redwood (key management).
- Identity providers supported: SAML (Okta), OIDC (Google Workspace, Azure AD).
- MFA requirement: All human users must use MFA (TOTP or hardware), enforced at IdP. Service-to-service uses short-lived mTLS certificates or OIDC service accounts.
- Roles (examples):
  - system-admin: Full administrative privileges. Used only by security and platform on-call.
  - infra-deployer: Can create/modify infra and deployment configs for non-production.
  - prod-deployer: Can perform canary and full rollouts to production; requires 2nd approver for high-risk services.
  - runbook-reader: Read-only access to runbooks and dashboards.
  - auditor: Read-only access to logs, audit datasets, and evidence catalog.

RBAC Evaluation & SLOs

- Policy eval latency SLO: policy-evaluator 99th percentile < 50ms for typical request path.
- Policy coverage: 100% of production endpoints must be covered by a policy or explicit allow list.
- Access review cadence: Quarterly access reviews for system-admin and prod-deployer roles.

Enforcement & Automation

- All role changes must be auditable and require PR + automated test that verifies intended policy change (pipeline: github -> policy CI -> deploy).
- Privileged access sessions (system-admin) are time-limited (default 1 hour) and require just-in-time elevation via the redwood-identity portal.
- Emergency access must be requested through the security on-call Slack flow and recorded in the evidence-catalog.

Authentication details

- Service accounts: issued as OIDC tokens with expiration <= 1 hour. Long-lived API keys are prohibited for new services.
- Secrets: stored in Vault with ACLs; database credentials are rotated every 30 days by rotator-job.

Audit Logging

- Collector & pipeline: app -> envoy sidecar (if applicable) -> logging-cluster (Kafka) -> auditor-service -> s3-compliance-bucket / AzureBlobEU / gcs-us (region-specific).
- What we log: authentication events (login, logout, MFA failures), privilege/grant changes, administrative actions (create/delete/modify infra), model-version rollouts, data exports, access to customer data, and API token usage.
- Log format: JSON lines with fields: timestamp, principal_id, principal_type (user/service), action, resource, resource_id, request_id, outcome, ip, region, trace_id, additional_context.

Retention & Access

- Default retention (non-PHI): 365 days.
- Customer-sensitive / compliance-critical retention: 7 years (per contract/legal requirement).
- Hot logs: 30 days in fast query store (Elasticsearch/managed equivalent) for alerting and investigations. Cold logs: remainder stored in write-once object store with integrity checks.
- Audit access: auditors and security have read-only access. Extracts for external auditors are created via evidence-catalog and must be approved by security.

Alerting & Monitoring

- Thresholds:
  - 5+ failed MFA attempts for a single account within 1 hour -> PagerDuty security-oncall (P1).
  - Unusual privilege grant (new system-admin) outside change window -> PagerDuty (P2) + automated suspend.
  - Bulk data export (>1GB within 1 hour) from customer-data buckets -> Security investigation workflow.

Data Residency & Retention Policies

- Regional controls: Services that serve EU-controlled customers must be pinned to EU regions (primary: eu-west-1, secondary: eu-central-1). Data-at-rest must use keys in the region (kms-redwood in-region).
- Data classification: PII, customer-content, telemetry, system-metadata. Owner (Product/Legal) must classify data in onboarding.
- Retention table (example):
  - telemetry: 90 days (aggregated long-term metrics retained as fingerprints up to 3 years).
  - system-metadata (non-sensitive): 1 year.
  - customer-content (per contract): 365 days default; 7+ years on request/contract.
  - audit-logs: 1 year default; 7 years for enterprise contracts.

- Data deletion (right-to-be-forgotten): Follow deletion-runbook; deletion requests create a ticket in the privacy queue and trigger delete jobs that verify object lifecycle and retention holds. Deletions are irreversible and recorded into the evidence-catalog.

Secure SDLC (Security in the software lifecycle)

Minimum gates for code deployment to production:
1. Code review: At least one approver from a different team for security-sensitive services.
2. Automated static analysis (SAST) in CI with zero-critical findings allowed.
3. Dependency scanning: No critical/urgent CVEs in direct dependencies; otherwise a mitigation plan with expiration must be filed.
4. Secret scanning: No secrets in the diff; CI rejects merges with detected secrets.
5. Infrastructure as Code checks: terraform plan must pass policy checks (rego/policy-evaluator).
6. Security integration tests: smoke test for auth flows and basic RBAC checks for affected services.

Additional controls:
- Pre-release security review required for model onboarding that involves customer data or private deployments.
- Canary rollouts: All production rollouts < 24 hours must start as canary (default 5% traffic) with automated rollback criteria.

Incident Response (security-specific)

Incident classification:
- Sev 1 (Security P1): Active exfiltration, compromised keys, or significant service compromise. Immediate PagerDuty escalation.
- Sev 2 (Security P2): Privilege escalation attempt, targeted account compromise, or suspicious high-volume data access.
- Sev 3 (Security P3): Low-risk anomalies, single-user suspicious activity.

High-level investigator playbook (short):
1. Triage & containment: Identify affected services, rotate keys (kms-redwood), isolate impacted hosts (cordon, remove from LB), and apply temporary ACLs.
2. Preserve evidence: Snapshot logs, mark evidence hold, and copy to evidence-catalog (read-only).
3. Communication: Security lead posts to incident channel, updates status page if customer impact, notifies legal if data breach.
4. Root cause analysis: Use traces (trace_id) and audit logs to reconstruct timeline.
5. Remediation & follow-up: Deploy fixes, rotate credentials, and produce postmortem with action items and owners.

- Escalation example: If an external attacker obtains a production API key, immediate actions include: revoke key, rotate service credentials, suspend affected service accounts, notify customers per legal requirements, open a breach response ticket.

Compliance Evidence Workflows

- Evidence sources: audit logs, access reviews, policy PRs (policy store history), infrastructure change logs, runbooks, training records, and contractual residency documentation.
- Evidence-catalog: Single source-of-truth (internal service: evidence-catalog) that stores metadata pointers to artifacts (S3 paths, PR links, snapshot IDs).
- Workflow:
  1. Initial request: Compliance or external auditor submits evidence request via the compliance UI or JIRA template.
  2. Triage: Security owner validates the scope, identifies artifacts, and assigns an evidence owner.
  3. Collection: Evidence owner exports signed snapshots and places them in s3-compliance-bucket with integrity checksum.
  4. Review & sign-off: Security and Legal approve the package; manifest is stored in evidence-catalog.
  5. Delivery: Provide auditor read-only link or create encrypted transfer (per legal requirements).

- Retention & attestations: Evidence packages for completed audits are retained for the contractually required period (commonly 7 years) and are tagged with audit-id, scope, and reviewers.

Risk & Exceptions Process

- When to request an exception: Temporary operational needs (legacy integration), blocked mitigations, or when a control materially impacts customer availability.
- Exception request steps:
  1. Submit exception form (Confluence template + risk assessment) to security@redwood.com.
  2. Include compensating controls, time-bound duration (max 90 days default), and rollback plan.
  3. Security reviews and either approve, approve-with-conditions, or deny.
  4. If approved, create a tracked ticket in risk-tracker with owner and expiry.
  5. Quarterly exception review to either close, extend (rare), or convert to remediation project.

- Example compensating controls: additional network ACLs, continuous audit watch with increased alerting, temporary read-only mode for affected features.

KPIs and Reporting

- KPIs: percent of production endpoints covered by RBAC (target 100%), mean time to detect (MTTD) for security incidents (target < 1 hour for Sev1), mean time to remediate (MTTR) for Sev1 (target < 8 hours), quarterly audit evidence delivery SLA (95% on-time).
- Reporting cadence: Monthly security metrics dashboard; quarterly access reviews and annual compliance attestations.
